taxonomic_note: Accepted in the current Kew/POWO Tradescantia backbone; learner retained at species rank.
look_here_first: Start at the base of the plant. Texas spiderwort is low, many-stemmed and bushy at ground level, with clearly hairy vegetative shoots; toward the inflorescence the hairs become strongly glandular. That compact, fuzzy architecture separates it quickly from the taller giant and prairie spiderworts.

project_inclusion.range_basis: UT Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium index; detailed Williamson County treatment; Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas explicit Bell County record.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Bell is counted only because the regional flora explicitly names the county; no ecoregion inference.

best_field_traits: compact ascending/spreading shoots, under 20 cm in the Williamson treatment
leaf blades pilose with hairs reaching several millimeters
inflorescence and pedicels conspicuously stalked-glandular hairy
terminal condensed cyme, usually 1–2 flowers open per day
morphology_keys.comparison_training: T. gigantea is taller and more robust with lower stems nearly glabrous. T. occidentalis is taller and grassier, with narrow leaves and especially conspicuous glandular stem/peduncle hairs. T. humilis stays low and bushy with hairy blades.
